hyps.why: Replacing a none on edge 3 restores a direct input-output path, giving larger gains than swapping one active op for another.
Adding a conv where edge 3 was removed reconnects the direct path and gains more than replacing an existing op.
With the direct edge 3 absent, removing edge 0 cuts the main route and hurts more.
With edge 3 absent, edge 5 is a key route into the output, so removing it costs more accuracy.
Filling an empty edge 1 adds a new path and gains more than swapping existing ops.
When edge 1 is none, node 2 depends on the path through edge 2, so a skip there helps more.
Activating an empty edge 4 adds capacity and a path, so it gains more than replacing an existing op.
Turning a none on the final edge into a conv can reconnect the output, giving a very large gain.
When edge 4 is none, removing edge 2 can leave node 3 disconnected from the input.
With edge 4 absent, fewer alternative routes exist, so removing edge 0 is more damaging.
